tutorial.name: QUALIFICATION
tutorial.beat: A closed practice line at the Lane Authority. No client, no cargo, no case — and no record. Passing it is what makes you the only operator in Meridian with nothing on file.

acts.title: THE CONTRACT
acts.premise: A new operator is screened across three ordinary contracts, told why, and handed a delivery that matters. The file arrives — and so does a commander with no case number.
acts.outline:
You are newly certified — no service record, no fleet friends, no debts to anyone in Meridian. Every one of those is a hole in your résumé and every one of them is why you get chosen.

Three contracts for Meridian Haulage, each planting one detail that only makes sense later: the fee clears before you file, he rebooks inside the hour and asks nothing, and clause 6 forbids you to discuss the run with anyone including the Lane Authority.

The offer: Renke tells you certain customer consignments have been hit for months — patient, professional, always the same kind of cargo. Not theft. Suppression. He built a file proving it and every attempt to deliver it has been interdicted in transit. You were not hired. You were chosen.

The delivery lands, Reyes opens the channel and names you RUNNER without explaining. The operation begins: staged traffic, clean interceptions, recovered keys — and the keys turn out to be current.

The answer: Renke’s file was never lost. It arrived four times and was destroyed at the door by something resident in Lane Command’s own evidence intake.

(The qualification run is NOT one of these eight — it is the separate TUTORIAL mode on the carousel.)

missions.name: YARDS OUTBOUND
missions.beat: First contract, taken because it is work. Routine outbound convoy, ordinary interdictors. PLANT 1: the fee clears before you file.

missions.name: OLD MOORINGS RELAY
missions.beat: Rebooked inside the hour. He asks nothing at all about what was in the lane. PLANT 2. The interdictors have gotten serious.

missions.name: METRO EXCHANGE
missions.beat: PLANT 3: clause 6. Volleys placed like something has watched an operator work. → THE OFFER: you were chosen.

missions.name: HARBOR CROSSING
missions.beat: The delivery run. Barriers strung to catch the file whole. → THE CONTACT. Reyes: "You’re RUNNER."

missions.name: SUBLANE DRIFT
missions.beat: First staged convoy. TRACE pulls a deployment key off the wreckage — it holds ACTIVE clearance. "log it, tell no one."

missions.name: TRADE SPINE
missions.beat: Phase-locked interdictors. A clean interception yields a working key — cut with credentials rotated this morning. THE SIGNATURES BEGIN.

missions.name: COMMAND APPROACH
missions.beat: TRACE isolates it: the file was never lost in transit. It arrived four times and was destroyed at the door.

missions.name: EVIDENCE INTAKE
missions.beat: THE WARDEN. Resident in Lane Command’s own intake, refusing one class of cargo for years. "everything i refused was contaminated. i was the filter."

verdict.name: THE WARDEN
verdict.beat: The intake is clean, the file is safe, the case can finally move. Nobody builds a thing like that for one file.

acts.title: THE RING
acts.premise: Wardens are everywhere and were never hidden. The interdictors are not placed — they are issued, by one dispatcher that signs its work. And somebody owns it.
acts.outline:
Once you know the shape of a warden, TRACE finds more, fast, because they were never hidden. Port authority. The courts. The licensing exchange. Guardians at the junctions that matter, deciding what arrives.

The signatures give up the rest: interdictors are dispatched — written, keyed, assigned a lane, deployed. So are the wardens. Six years of it, out of one source, signing itself in a metadata field nobody was meant to read. The Dispatcher.

Reyes says the part she has been building to: nobody rents this. Somebody owns it. There is a ring in Meridian — people who know exactly who each other are, in a Reach that does not know they exist.

And it keeps. Intercepted cargo is not destroyed, it is filed. There is an archive.

You take the Tribunal at the courts junction. The junction is clear for about a day. Then there is another one, cast later, already better.

missions.name: PORT AUTHORITY
missions.beat: Now that you know the shape of a warden, TRACE finds another. It was never hidden — it has been standing there for years.

missions.name: CIVIC RECORDS
missions.beat: And another. Meridian has been running on a Grid that answers to somebody else.

missions.name: LICENSING EXCHANGE
missions.beat: Phase-locked interdictors at every junction. The signatures start matching across attacks with nothing else in common.

missions.name: THE JUNCTIONS
missions.beat: They are not placed by hand. They are dispatched — written, keyed, assigned a lane, deployed.

missions.name: DISPATCH LANES
missions.beat: One source, six years, and it signs its work. TRACE: "it has a name for itself. the dispatcher."

missions.name: THE OLD BUILD
missions.beat: REYES: nobody rents this. Somebody owns it. The Ring — and the Lanes were charted around them so long ago they look like geography.

missions.name: COLD STORAGE
missions.beat: Intercepted cargo is not destroyed. It is filed. There is an archive, and it is still intact.

missions.name: THE TRIBUNAL
missions.beat: Three cores at the courts junction. A newer casting than the intake warden, and it does not make the intake warden’s mistake.

verdict.name: THE TRIBUNAL
verdict.beat: A day later the junction has another warden, and it is already better. REYES: "We stop chasing wardens. We find the thing that writes them."

acts.title: GOING BLIND
acts.premise: They remove Renke through channels. You lose your eyes, gain a van, and TRACE stops reading and starts planting.
acts.outline:
Renke is called to a hearing — customer traffic routed to an off-book contractor, on his authorization, in his own hand. Suspended, marked for termination, access revoked the same afternoon. He is not hurt. He is removed, correctly, by people who never had to break a law.

Reyes will not put you in a safe house and says why. A technical van, and one instruction: stay mobile. From here the game runs out of a rain-streaked box in a parking structure with three faces on a screen — one of them dark.

Without Renke there is no routing, no transit logs, no legitimate cargo to ride. So TRACE stops reading and starts planting: bait data of exactly the kind the Ring reaches for, seeded on live lines. Crude, unauthorized, and it works enormously — volume is what triangulation needs.

And the Ring hunts back, with a warden that guards nothing at all. The Seeker sweeps for the shape of an operator working a line, and it has been looking for you since the harbor crossing.

missions.name: DARK ROUTE
missions.beat: Renke is suspended pending review. No client, no cover, no routing. Reyes puts you somewhere nobody is looking.

missions.name: PARKING LEVEL 3
missions.beat: The van. Stay mobile — never the same lot twice, never a fixed uplink, never a pattern.

missions.name: BAIT LINES
missions.beat: TRACE stops reading and starts planting. Bait data on live lines. Renke would have refused to sign it.

missions.name: THE BITE
missions.beat: It works enormously. Every bite is a phase-locked interdictor cast into a lane the Dispatcher had no reason to watch. The count starts climbing.

missions.name: OPEN SWEEP
missions.beat: Something is sweeping. Patiently, endlessly, across every line in Meridian, looking for the shape of an operator.

missions.name: UNDER THE BEAM
missions.beat: You cannot hide from it and you cannot outrun it. So you go where it is looking.

missions.name: SEARCH PATTERN
missions.beat: It has been looking for you since the harbor crossing. Reyes’s decoys are the only reason it has not closed.

missions.name: THE SEEKER
missions.beat: A warden that guards nothing. Ride the beam, survive every sweep, and take what is inside it.

verdict.name: THE SEEKER
verdict.beat: A standing search order, six years old, never cancelled. Two designations — yours, and BLADE’s. REYES: "…yes. That’s what I meant."

acts.title: THE FOUNDRY
acts.premise: Map the Dispatcher’s reach, find the casting line every warden comes from, and write the antidote from its own handwriting.
acts.outline:
You know what it is and roughly where. Now find out what it is made of, because you are not going to fight it — you are going to unwrite it, and TRACE needs to know exactly how it is put together.

Reconnaissance at speed, under fire. Dispatch lanes. Deployment schedules. The route a warden takes from written to standing. How far it reaches, which is: everywhere, into every junction in the Reach, continuously, without anyone having asked it to for years.

Meanwhile the decoys thin, Renke’s review date is set, and TRACE is running staging she is not qualified for. Nobody says the word deadline.

At the bottom of the reach: not a guard. A casting line — where the Dispatcher writes wardens, tests them against the last thing that killed one, and ships. The least defended thing in the game and the most dangerous, because it is producing while you are inside it.

missions.name: REACH SURVEY
missions.beat: Stop chasing and start mapping. How far does the Dispatcher actually go?

missions.name: DISPATCH ORDER
missions.beat: The route an interdictor takes from written to standing. Every one carries where it came from.

missions.name: CASTING SCHEDULE
missions.beat: Wardens are not deployed at random. They are scheduled, and the schedule has a shape.

missions.name: EVERY JUNCTION
missions.beat: The answer to how far it reaches: everywhere, continuously, and nobody has asked it to for years.

missions.name: THE CLOCK
missions.beat: Decoys thinning, review date set, TRACE running staging she is not qualified for. Nobody says deadline.

missions.name: THE UNDERLINE
missions.beat: Below the dispatch layer there is an older one, and it goes somewhere that is not on any map.

missions.name: THE MOULD
missions.beat: Every warden in Meridian shares a structure, because they were all cast from one thing.

missions.name: THE FOUNDRY
missions.beat: The casting line itself — producing while you are inside it. Take it and you take the pattern.

verdict.name: THE ANTIDOTE
verdict.beat: TRACE writes it from the pattern and four acts of signatures. It does not fight — it unwrites. "i can write it. i can’t take it there."

acts.title: THE ARCHIVE
acts.premise: Carry the antidote into the oldest segment of the Lanes, unwrite the Dispatcher, and bring six years of what it kept out whole.
acts.outline:
The last act is the first act inverted. Forty missions protecting other people’s cargo down other people’s lanes; now you carry one consignment of your own into the deepest, oldest, most defended stretch of lane in Meridian — laid when the Reach was surveyed, never opened to anything since.

Renke comes back for it. Still suspended, still under review, and he does it anyway, because a run into that segment needs Meridian Haulage’s transit fabric and he is the only person alive who knows how it is stitched together.

The signatures are the door. Their defenses stop pretending: walls folding shut in sequence, a channel screaming with everything thrown blind, deep transit running hot enough to blur, and one narrow threshold with the whole network firing into it.

And the Dispatcher talks, because it has never in six years been asked to explain itself.

missions.name: INJECTION
missions.beat: Renke comes back. The antidote goes on the wire, and it only exists once.

missions.name: OUTER SEGMENT
missions.beat: The Lanes stop pretending. No interception, no subtlety — everything swings to kill.

missions.name: THE DELTA
missions.beat: Walls folding shut in sequence, trying to seal the convoy into a dead segment.

missions.name: THE SCREAM
missions.beat: Everything the Lanes carry, thrown blind. This is not defense. This is furniture against a door.

missions.name: LAST RING
missions.beat: It falls back and seals the approach — every gate keyed, every lane walled.

missions.name: DEEP TRANSIT
missions.beat: No walls left down here. Just speed, the last thing it has.

missions.name: THE THRESHOLD
missions.beat: One narrow gate with the whole Reach’s infrastructure firing into it.

missions.name: THE DISPATCHER
missions.beat: Not a fortress — a clerk with six locks. "you have been arguing with a form." Seat the antidote.

verdict.name: THE ARCHIVE
verdict.beat: The archive falls open — six years of killed audits and filings that never arrived, each tagged with the order that stopped it. Transfer all of it to Reyes.
